text.p: Flextronics International Ltd said Tuesday that revenues for its fourth quarter ended March 31, 1997 were $128.7 million, up from $121.5 million in the third quarter and $125.7 million in the comparable year ago quarter.

The company said in a statement that it is not releasing the rest of its results at this time because of discussions with the Securities and Exchange Commission to resolve the accounting for its January 1996 acquisition of Astron Technologies.

In accounting for the acquisition Flextronics obtained an appraisal of Astron's in-process technologies from an independent valuation firm. Much of the company's discussions with the SEC have related to this appraisal. Flextronics has undertaken to obtain a second independent valuation of various elements of the assets of Astron and has engaged an international appraisal firm for this purpose.

In addition, the SEC has said that a $14 million payment due to Stephen Rees, the former chairman of Astron, in June 30, 1998 should be accounted as part of the purchase price for Astron and not as compensation. The company anticipates that obtaining a new appraisal and completing discussions with the SEC will take from one to two months.

"Flextronics had a very strong March quarter," said Michael Marks, chief executive officer. "Our new facility in southern Sweden is coming up to speed rapidly and is putting us in a strong position to serve our customers in the European market. We are also making good progress with expansions in China, Mexico and San Jose."
